answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to carry a cipher-bound work history: every completed job is signed and linked into a grove of attestations from distinct, already-established peers, so reputation grows only by branching outward through real counterparties. A fresh identity starts at its nadir with zero weight, and creating thousands of sock puppets gains nothing, because weight comes from verified past work, not from the number of accounts — an attacker must pay the full cost of genuine service for each fake reputation, which makes mass forgery uneconomical.
